# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,

impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. blocks.text:
# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

blocks.text:
# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. blocks.text:
# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

## PR Description

Closes #1025

## What changed
- `js/common/machineAuthor.js`: `stripBotSuffix()` — one trailing `[bot]` (case-insensitive) is normalized away on BOTH sides of the comparison in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`. Configured `dmtools-factory-bot` now matches the API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Bare-login case-sensitivity in `isMachineAuthored` is preserved (design); `robot` is never stripped to `ro`; a different bot never matches.
- `sm_github.json`: `conflict-rework` limit 1 → 5 — an already-reported DIRTY PR consumed the whole per-tick slot every tick (live: #983 parked the approved trio #1014/#1016/#1018). Marker dedup keeps re-reports idempotent.
- 7 new tests in `test_machineAuthor.js` (written red-first per TDD).

## Root cause (live evidence, SM tick 39103844372, 2026-10-18 06:24Z)
#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the `machineAuthor` list, but GitHub reports App authors as `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` — exact match never fired → every `prMachineAuthor` rule fail-closed for ~8h: no rework legs (last AI Teammate run 22:52Z), #1017's 9 unresolved machine threads probed-then-dropped, the DIRTY approved trio reported-but-never-armed. Reviews masked the outage (`review-after-dev` has no machineAuthor gate).

# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```

blocks.text:
# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. blocks.text:
# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. blocks.text:
# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

  "fields": {
    "summary": "machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead",
    "description": "## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```"

blocks.text:
# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

## PR Description

Closes #1025

## What changed
- `js/common/machineAuthor.js`: `stripBotSuffix()` — one trailing `[bot]` (case-insensitive) is normalized away on BOTH sides of the comparison in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`. Configured `dmtools-factory-bot` now matches the API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Bare-login case-sensitivity in `isMachineAuthored` is preserved (design); `robot` is never stripped to `ro`; a different bot never matches.
- `sm_github.json`: `conflict-rework` limit 1 → 5 — an already-reported DIRTY PR consumed the whole per-tick slot every tick (live: #983 parked the approved trio #1014/#1016/#1018). Marker dedup keeps re-reports idempotent.
- 7 new tests in `test_machineAuthor.js` (written red-first per TDD).

## Root cause (live evidence, SM tick 39103844372, 2026-10-18 06:24Z)
#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the `machineAuthor` list, but GitHub reports App authors as `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` — exact match never fired → every `prMachineAuthor` rule fail-closed for ~8h: no rework legs (last AI Teammate run 22:52Z), #1017's 9 unresolved machine threads probed-then-dropped, the DIRTY approved trio reported-but-never-armed. Reviews masked the outage (`review-after-dev` has no machineAuthor gate).

## How to verify
```bash

# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

{
  "key": "gh-1025",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead",
    "description": "## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```"

blocks.text:
# gh-1025: machineAuthor exact-match misses GitHub App [bot] suffix — every prMachineAuthor SM rule fail-closed, all rework/review arms dead

## Description

## Symptom (live, 2026-10-18 ~06:24Z, SM tick 39103844372)

Since PR #988 merged (17:58Z), **no machine-gated SM rule matches anything**: no rework legs dispatch, no `agent:rework` arms land, conflict-rework reports but never arms. Every tick processes 0-1 items and the queue is silently dead while labels look armed.

## Root cause

`js/common/machineAuthor.js` `isMachineAuthored` / `isMachineLogin` compare author logins **exactly** against the configured list:

```
machineAuthor: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot'
```

but GitHub's REST API reports GitHub App authors **with the `[bot]` suffix**: PRs #1017/#1014/#983 etc. carry `author = dmtools-factory-bot[bot]`. Exact match fails → `prMachineAuthor: true` gates fail closed on every rule:

- `rework-on-red-ci` — gh-960 has `agent:rework` armed + open machine PR #983, query returns "No tickets found" every tick → **no rework leg since 22:52Z** (last AI Teammate run on the repo).
- `rework-unresolved-threads` — #1017 has 9 unresolved machine threads; the source probes the threads (visible in the log) and then the machineAuthor gate drops it → never armed.
- `conflict-rework` action — arms `agent:rework` only for machine-authored PRs; with the broken match the DIRTY approved trio (#1014/#1016/#1018) gets "report only" treatment, issues gh-1005/1007/1011 never receive `agent:rework`.
- Reviews kept working only because `review-after-dev` has no `prMachineAuthor` gate — that's why the failure was invisible.

#988 added `dmtools-factory-bot` to the list but without the `[bot]` suffix, so it never actually matched.

## Fix

Normalize the `[bot]` suffix (case-insensitive) on BOTH sides of the comparison — a configured `dmtools-factory-bot` must match API-reported `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (and vice versa). Exact-match semantics for non-bot logins unchanged.

## Secondary (same wedge class): conflict-rework limit-1 starvation

`conflict-rework` (`limit: 1`) counts the *already-reported* DIRTY PR against its per-tick limit: #983 logs "conflict already reported for head — waiting on rework" and consumes the slot **every tick**, so #1014/#1016/#1018 are never even evaluated. Already-reported candidates must not consume the limit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dmtools-factory-bot` (configured) matches `dmtools-factory-bot[bot]` (API) in `isMachineAuthored` and `isMachineLogin`; tests cover both directions + non-bot exactness preserved.
- [ ] gh-960's armed `agent:rework` dispatches a rework leg on the next tick after deploy.
- [ ] #1017 arms `agent:rework` for its 9 unresolved machine threads.
- [ ] conflict-rework no longer starves later DIRTY PRs behind an already-reported one.

## How to verify

```bash
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_machineAuthor.js
```

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
